title: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes with Butter and Maple Syrup
summary: A lumpy buttermilk and soured cream batter, rested briefly, makes tall, tender pancakes cooked on a lightly oiled pan and kept warm in a low oven.
equipment: 30 cm non-stick frying pan or griddle
wire rack set in a baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly

steps.title: Warm the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 100 °C (80 °C fan) and put the wire rack and tray inside. This keeps the first pancakes warm without drying them while you cook the rest.

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt in one bowl so the raising agents are evenly spread.

steps.title: Mix the wet ingredients
steps.text: In the second bowl, whisk the buttermilk, soured cream, eggs and melted butter until smooth.

steps.title: Combine and rest
steps.text: Make a well in the dry ingredients, pour in the wet mixture and fold gently with the spatula until just combined, leaving lumps and a few streaks of flour. Rest for 10 minutes. Overmixing develops the gluten and makes pancakes tough, while resting lets the flour hydrate and the bubbles start to form.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in the pan over medium heat until shimmering, then wipe it out with kitchen paper to leave only a thin film. Too much oil gives blotchy, greasy pancakes.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pour in 60 ml batter per pancake, 4 at a time. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the edges look set, the base is golden and bubbles on top are starting to burst. Flip and cook for 1-2 minutes more, until golden underneath and the centre springs back when pressed.

steps.title: Keep warm
steps.text: Move the pancakes to the rack in the oven and repeat with the remaining batter, adding a little oil when the pan looks dry. You should get about 16 pancakes, 10 cm across.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Stack 4 pancakes on each plate and top with a little butter and the maple syrup.

tips: Flipping too early is the commonest mistake; wait until bubbles break on the surface and the edges look dry.
If the first pancake browns before the bubbles appear, turn the heat down a little.
Keep the pancakes on a rack, not stacked on a plate, or they steam and turn soggy.
Don't press pancakes flat with the spatula, or you'll squeeze out the air.
storage: Cool, then refrigerate for up to 2 days or freeze, layered with baking paper, for up to 1 month. Reheat in a toaster or a 180 °C oven until hot. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
